headline: Nvidia Slips While the Wider Market Climbs in Early Black Friday Trade
body_html:
Nvidia is the stock the market is talking about in early Friday trading, and not for a flattering reason. The chip giant was down 2.02% even as the broader market pushed higher. Recent coverage points to lingering investor unease over leadership questions at the company, along with reports that its Blackwell chips have turned up at a site in China. Together they keep the biggest name in AI on the defensive.

Around it, the tape is firm. The S&P 500 was up 0.86% and the Nasdaq up 1.17%, with 481 stocks rising and 178 falling in a universe of 661. Energy led the sectors, up 2.24%, as oil headed to end a three-week losing streak on supply worries. Technology rose 1.44%, materials 1.19% and semiconductors 1.03%, while healthcare was flat. Tesla climbed 3.56% and Broadcom 2.03%.

Prices are not final. Black Friday is a half-day, with U.S. markets closing early at 1:00 p.m. ET, so the session is short. Watch whether Nvidia steadies while the rest of the chip group advances, whether energy holds its gains, and how the early close shapes the final hour. The next trading day is Monday, November 30.

briefs.headline: Tesla Leads the Mega-Caps Higher
briefs.body: Tesla rose 3.56% in early trading, the strongest move among the largest companies. Coverage highlights its Dallas robotaxi zone growing 83.5% and a European Union vote on self-driving technology set for December 15, a date investors are watching closely.

briefs.headline: Memory Names Pace the Chip Rally
briefs.body: Sandisk jumped 8.99%, the top gain in the universe, and Micron added 2.33%. The strength in memory helped lift the semiconductor group, which was up 1.03% on average, even with Nvidia lower.

briefs.headline: Energy Is the Best Sector as Oil Eyes a Turn
briefs.body: Energy stocks averaged a 2.24% gain, the best of any sector. Crude was on track to snap a three-week losing streak on supply fears, with reports that Washington has urged Venezuela and Iraq to consider leaving OPEC adding to the focus on supply.

briefs.headline: Vertex Pharmaceuticals Drops Sharply
briefs.body: Vertex Pharmaceuticals fell 7.84%, the largest decline in the universe. TG Therapeutics also lost 2.92%. Healthcare was flat on average, so the weakness was concentrated in individual names rather than the whole sector.

briefs.headline: Space Stocks Catch a Bid
briefs.body: Intuitive Machines rose 6.56% and MDA Space gained 5.82%, putting both among the early leaders. Coherent, an optical networking name, was also strong, up 8.44%, and Lasertec rose 7.43%.

briefs.headline: Airline Distress Adds a Cautionary Note
briefs.body: The Norwegian operating unit of Norse Atlantic has filed for bankruptcy as the conflict involving Iran strains airlines. Separately, with inflation pushing shoppers toward bargains, early Black Friday commentary suggests value-focused retailers could benefit.
